title: Hybrid token-shed policy with predictive KV soft-release and model-tier fallback
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Problem: Frequent GPU OOMs observed on mixed sequence-length workloads when continuous batching interacts with an aggressively sized KV cache. Root cause analysis shows three contributing factors: (1) long-lived KV entries from high-cardinality prefixes that block memory reclamation, (2) unbounded batch growth during short traffic spikes, and (3) lack of kernel-aware memory budgeting per model variant. When OOMs occur we see large tail latency spikes and failed requests that require customer-visible retries or fallbacks.

Goal: Add a memory-safe, graceful degradation path that (A) proactively reduces GPU memory pressure before OOMs, (B) preserves QoE for high-value requests, and (C) supports automated fallback to smaller model tiers or CPU-mode execution with minimal loss of throughput.

Proposed solution (high level):
1) Predictive KV soft-release: extend KV manager with a probabilistic heatmap that scores KV entries by recent token re-use and predicted near-term access. Lower-scoring entries are marked for soft-release (eviction candidates) but kept in a fast spill cache (sharded host memory) for quick rehydrate. Soft-release is non-blocking and prioritized by request criticality tag.

2) Hybrid token-shed admission: implement an admission controller that performs progressive token-shedding on batched requests when memory headroom dips below thresholds. Token shedding is staged: reduce speculative tokens (e.g., sampling logits cache), then shrink per-request max_tokens, then selectively trim low-priority requests in the batch (based on customer QoS tag). Shedding should aim for minimal semantic degradation (prefer removing trailing padding or low-confidence continuation).

3) Kernel-aware memory budgeting: expose per-model and per-variant memory budgets to the scheduler. The serving runtime will enforce a soft cap and reserve a safety pool to satisfy immediate KV re-inflation. Budgets adapt based on observed sequence-length distributions and kernel footprint heuristics (attention memory, kv storage).

4) Model-tier fallback policy: when shedding + soft-release cannot recover headroom, route new requests to a compatible smaller quantized variant or to a CPU-based fallback pool. Routing decisions include a quick lookup of model compatibility and an automatic rollback if the fallback variant produces unacceptable quality (monitored via a small prompt-level evaluator).

5) Retry and backoff semantics: orchestrate retries for affected requests with exponential backoff and jitter. Retries prefer rerouting over recollecting on the same GPU where OOM occurred. Ensure idempotency semantics are preserved for streaming vs non-streaming requests.

Implementation notes and tasks:
- KV manager: implement heatmap scoring, host-spill fast-path, and soft-release API. Add param: kv_soft_release_ratio.
- Admission layer: add token-shed controller in batch admission path with progressive stages and pluggable priority function.
- Scheduler: per-model budget metadata, enforcement hooks, and safety pool allocator.
- Fallback layer: extend routing table for variant matching, add quality gating hook using lightweight evals.
- Config/flags: feature flag "hybrid-token-shed-v1" + tunables for thresholds.
- Tests: unit tests for KV scoring, integration tests for shedding behavior under synthetic traffic, chaos tests that inject OOMs and validate fallback correctness.

Performance targets and acceptance criteria:
- OOM incidence rate across canary fleet reduced to <0.1% per 24h.
- P99 latency increase during shedding windows <= 15% compared to baseline.
- Fallback success (request completed via fallback route) >= 98% when primary path rejects due to memory.
- No silent correctness regressions: small evaluator quality delta < 3% for fallback variants on sampled prompts.

Observability changes:
- New metrics: kv_heatmap_distribution, kv_soft_releases/sec, token_shed_events, memory_budget_headroom, fallback_routed_requests, fallback_quality_failures.
- Tracing: annotate traces with token-shed stage, kv_release_id, and fallback_variant.
- Dashboards: OOM resilience dashboard for per-cluster headroom, shedding events, and quality gate pass rate.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (dev): unit + integration tests, local e2e with synthetic spike driver.
- Phase 1 (canary small subset): enable feature flag on 5% of serving capacity in us-west1 with aggressive telemetry.
- Phase 2 (wider ramp): 25% -> 60% with tuned thresholds. Monitor metrics and evaluator.
- Phase 3 (ga): enable by default with operator overrides for enterprise customers.

Dependencies and blockers:
- Requires kernel memory footprint model from infra (ENG-48201) for budgeting heuristics.
- Host-spill fast-path depends on a sharded host-memory allocator being available (ENG-41756).
- Need QA test harness for injecting controlled OOMs (follow-up infra ticket planned).

Notes on trade-offs:
- Soft-release keeps data in host memory which increases host RAM usage and potential latency on rehydrate; trade-off acceptable to avoid hard OOMs.
- Token shedding risks degraded generation quality; mitigation is staged shedding and QoS tagging to protect high-value requests.
- Fallback to smaller models reduces cost predictability; include cost accounting and user-visible routing logs.

Deliverables:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/Hybrid+Token+Shed+Design
- Implementation PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pulls?q=is%3Apr+hybrid-token-shed
- Canary dashboard: internal link (Grafana): /d/oom-resilience/hybrid-token-shed-canary
acceptance_criteria: 1) Deployment reduces OOMs <0.1%/24h; 2) p99 latency increase <=15% during shedding; 3) Fallback route completes >=98% of requests when used; 4) Observability emits the new metrics and traces; 5) QA chaos tests pass (inject OOMs and verify graceful degradation)
observability_changes: Emit kv_heatmap_distribution, kv_soft_releases/sec, token_shed_events, memory_budget_headroom, fallback_routed_requests, fallback_quality_failures. Add trace tags: token_shed_stage, kv_release_id, fallback_variant. Add Grafana dashboard and SLO alerts for OOM rate and fallback quality failures.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): unit+integration tests. Phase 1 (canary 5%): enable via feature flag in us-west1. Phase 2 (ramp 25%->60%): tune thresholds. Phase 3 (GA): default on with operator override. Rollback path: disable feature flag and evacuate soft-released KV back to GPU on stable windows.
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: rehydrate latency spikes from host spill. Mitigation: prioritize synchronous rehydration for active requests and background reclamation for cold entries.
Risk: fallback variants produce unacceptable hallucinations. Mitigation: quality gate and immediate rollback of routing decisions based on evaluator feedback.
Risk: increased host memory pressure. Mitigation: add host memory monitoring and per-node host-spill caps.
